question: Derive the expression for fringe width in Young’s double-slit experiment. Hence explain how the fringe width changes when the screen distance is doubled and the slit separation is kept unchanged.

options.A: For a point at distance $x$, $\Delta x=d\sin\theta\approx\dfrac{dx}{D}$. For a bright fringe, $\Delta x=n\lambda$, so $x_n=\dfrac{n\lambda D}{d}$. Hence $\beta=x_{n+1}-x_n=\dfrac{\lambda D}{d}$. If $D$ is doubled while $d$ is unchanged, $\beta'=\dfrac{\lambda(2D)}{d}=2\beta$.
options.B: The fringe width is $\beta=\dfrac{d}{\lambda D}$. Therefore, doubling the screen distance makes fringe width half.
options.C: The fringe width is $\beta=\dfrac{\lambda d}{D}$. Therefore, doubling screen distance makes the width one-fourth.
options.D: The fringe width is independent of screen distance because only slit separation determines the fringe pattern.
